title: Took over the repo and the paper
detail: Cloned rikhil-amonkar/solver-like-behavior-in-llms, read the code and the submitted paper.

title: Meeting Planning is actually checked
detail: The old evaluator accepted any non-empty list. It now replays each itinerary against travel times, availability windows and minimum durations, and must meet as many friends as the gold plan. GPT-OSS Meeting baseline fell from 0.93 to 0.66.

title: BlocksWorld validated against the gold PDDL
detail: The evaluator received an empty problem, so plan_exists and the gold PDDL were never used. Now Fast Downward plans the model's PDDL and VAL checks the plan under the gold domain and problem.

title: The executed program is the final answer's
detail: Qwen ran a draft from inside its thinking in 16-25% of examples; code after the end-of-thinking marker now wins.

title: All 36 runs re-scored; RQ3 reworded
detail: Correlation of ratio change with accuracy change moved from -0.07 to -0.42, driven by GPT-OSS Meeting. Paper table and RQ3 text updated.

title: First open-judge check (Gemma 4 31B)
detail: 20 blind chunks: Harry agreed with Gemini 14/20 and with Gemma 13/20, far below the paper's 95%. Led to rethinking the judge.

title: Batch judge order bug fixed
detail: Vertex batch outputs were matched to examples by position, but come back shuffled. Gemini chunk labels re-keyed: 1,926 of 3,600 traces fully repaired, 1,313 partly, 361 not.

title: Rule-based hardcoding checker (RQ4)
detail: Matches human labels on 30/30 programs. GPT-OSS Meeting hardcoded programs: 52/93 baseline, 13/93 Caut A, 6/89 Caut B. RQ4 added to the paper.

title: Gemma re-judge with the old prompt (stopped)
detail: Fixed Gemma looping on long segments (6k to 2k tokens: loops 83% to 7%). Stopped at 48% to refine how judging works.

title: Three Qwen runs redone on vLLM
detail: Calendar baseline/Caut A and Meeting baseline had been generated with a different engine and temperature. A code-extractor bug (lines starting with 'wait') was also fixed. Qwen Meeting is now 0.88/0.85/0.93.

title: Solver-like behavior ontology adopted
detail: Replaces the single sound/solver-like label with per-node judges: A (solving in prose), B (what the program does with it), C (agreement). Refined after a sweep of 107 traces. Paper Section 3 and Figure 2.

title: A judge tuned against Harry's labels
detail: Prompt versions v2 to v12 over three blind rounds of 70 paragraphs. Chosen gemma_v11t: 66/70, Values precision and recall 20/22. A2 checks 20/20 and 19/20.

title: B judge chosen and run on everything
detail: gemma_b5t: 19/20 against Claude's blind labels; Harry confirmed 20/20 on held-out programs. Full B run over 3,591 programs finished at 15:05 UTC.

title: Ontology frozen
detail: Values only: properties, the with-search flag, A3 purpose and the specification-change flag were dropped.

title: Paper rewritten around the ontology
detail: Ontology definitions with examples, per-node judges and reliability in Metrics and a new appendix, models run with vLLM at 131k tokens.

title: Cross-FL experiment designed
detail: Calendar in Z3-Python and ZebraLogic in plain Python separate the dataset from the formal language. --fl flag added and smoke-tested.

title: Cross-FL runs launched: every dataset in two FLs
detail: Calendar and Meeting in Z3-Python, ZebraLogic and BlocksWorld in plain Python. DeepSeek running over the API; Qwen and GPT-OSS queued on GPU 7. BlocksWorld plans from Python programs are validated with VAL.

title: FL compliance flagged on every run
detail: Decided with Harry: flag and report the rate, also on native runs. Native: 3 of ~2,600 programs not in their FL (truncated Z3 sketches). Execution now records fl_compliance per program.

title: Native runs fully judged
detail: A (gemma_v11t, 29,237 segments), B (gemma_b5t, 3,591 programs) and A2/C (gemma_v11c, 3,600 traces) cover every native trace; nothing missing or stale.

title: Cross-FL runs done for DeepSeek and GPT-OSS
detail: 12 runs each (four new pairings x 3 conditions). Accuracy close to the native FL; Meeting-Z3's lower golden accuracy was a prompt-format artefact, now normalised.
